opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: [bounty $400] Implement ABNF-compliant email address parser with full §3.2–§4.4 coverage
opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. This parser must handle every edge case defined in the RFC — not just simple `user@domain` patterns, but the full complexity of quoted strings, comments, folding whitespace, group addresses, and domain literals. ## Background RFC 5322 defines email address syntax through a chain of ABNF productions that build on each other: ``` address = mailbox / group mailbox = name-addr / addr-spec name-addr = [display-name] angle-addr angle-addr = [CFWS] "<" addr-spec ">" [CFWS] addr-spec = local-part "@" domain local-part = dot-atom / quoted-string / obs-local-part domain = dot-atom / domain-literal / obs-domain ``` Each of these references further productions (CFWS, FWS, quoted-pair, dtext, etc.) that span multiple sections. **You must read `source.md` completely** to trace the full grammar dependency chain. ## Requirements ### 1. opportunities.title: Wayfinder task: reward calibration — margin→win-prob fitted on ladder corpus, proven by decision-tier verdict
opportunities.summary: Map: #1892 ## Question Execute attack-order step 3 (research #1894, harness #1924): replace the hand-set linear-clip reward mapping (`rewardFromValue`, `MATERIAL_FULL = 500`, `TERMINAL_BAND = 0.25` in `convex/gre/search.ts`) with a **margin → win-probability mapping calibrated on self-play outcomes**, and prove it with a ladder verdict. This is the highest-leverage change the telemetry identified: 99.5% of real decisions sit inside the current 100-margin-point indifference band (#1893). This is a task ticket — the design is locked (logistic/isotonic fit per `docs/research/mcts-small-budget-strength.md`; A/B discipline per #1895). Steps: 1. **Corpus + noise floor**: launch a `decision`-tier NULL run (`bun run ladder --tier decision`) in an isolated slot (~4–5h). Its JSONL is the calibration corpus (per-game final margins + outcomes are already recorded; extend the record with mid-game margin samples if needed) AND the harness noise-floor measurement (aggregate CI must straddle 50%). 2. **Fit**: margin → P(win) on that corpus (logistic in margin is the default; check calibration curve). Deterministic, in-repo fitting script; fitted constants land as code, not a data file dependency.
